newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles police chief's fate sealed by council.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles police chief's fate sealed by council.

text.p: The fate of embattled Los Angeles police chief Willie Williams was sealed Wednesday when his chief backer on the city council backed off in her efforts to save his job.

The Los Angeles Police Commission, a civilian body, decided last week not to rehire Williams for a second five-year term as chief of police in America's second-largest city. Councilwoman Rita Walters had vowed to overturn that decision through the Los Angeles City Council.

But Wednesday, announcing that she did not have the two-thirds majority needed from the 15-member council to keep Williams in office, Walters instead moved that a severance package be worked out for the police chief.

Williams, brought in from Philadelphia in 1992 as a "model" chief to revamp a department sullied by the police beating of black motorist Rodney King and the riots that ensued when the four white officers involved were cleared of wrongdoing by a jury, was given a poor rating by the police commission when it evaluated his job performance.
The commission, in turning down the chief's second term, said it had problems with Williams' management ability and his integrity -- sentiments expressed by a number of council members.

Williams, the first black to serve as Los Angeles Police Chief, has said that he would serve out his first term, which ends July 6. But council members said they expected him to leave office earlier with a severance package, opening the way for another black, Deputy Chief Bernard Parks, to become interim chief until another leader is appointed.
According to reports, Williams is negotiating a buyout anywhere between $100,000 and $3 million.
